findings.text: Polling input first invokes the quiesce helper to lower interrupts, then samples receive-empty state from the flag register. If empty it reports NO_POLL_CHAR, otherwise it returns the byte from the data register. The routine expects the polling caller to own transmit queue management.

Polling output waits until the transmit-full indication clears from the flag register, relaxing the CPU while waiting, then writes the supplied byte to the data register. It performs no interrupt manipulation and assumes the caller already owns the device.

Interrupt quiescing acknowledges currently pending sources observed through the masked status register via the clear register, then masks the transmit-ready enable while leaving other enables unchanged. Transmit-ready cannot be cleared, only masked, and the transmit start path is expected to unmask it later.

Quiescing can race with concurrent transmit start, so the polling user may observe another interrupt immediately after clearing. The design treats this as benign because fresh controller activity can raise an interrupt even without a race, and polling users are assumed to manage the device including the transmit queue.

Hardware initialization selects the default pin state, enables the clock and records the current rate as the UART clock. It clears receive and timeout pendings together with overrun, framing, parity and break error pendings, saves the current interrupt mask, then enables only receive timeout and receive to support NMI entry, and runs an optional platform init hook. Clock enable failure aborts before further programming.

Split line-control hardware is detected by comparing receive and transmit control register offsets. When they differ, configuration writes the receive side first, delays through repeated writes to a read-only status register, then writes the transmit side with the same value. Unified hardware receives a single write.

Interrupt allocation restores the previously saved software mask into hardware before requesting a shared interrupt line for the UART, associating the generic handler and the port private state with the port IRQ number.

Interrupt enabling holds the port lock with interrupts saved. While holding it the driver clears spurious timeout and receive pendings, drains any bytes already present in the receive FIFO, then programs a mask containing timeout and, unless DMA reception is active, receive.

When the receive FIFO already sits above its trigger threshold the level indication will not reassert and would remain stuck off. The driver prevents this by explicitly draining up to twice the FIFO depth until empty is observed before enabling interrupts.

Normal startup chains hardware init and IRQ allocation, programs FIFO trigger levels, then under lock preserves modem outputs while enabling the UART plus receive and, unless RS485 mode is active, transmit. It snapshots modem status from flag lines, starts DMA, then enables interrupts, with clock or IRQ failure disabling the clock and aborting. The SBSA variant omits trigger programming, control programming, modem sampling and DMA, instead zeroing modem state before enabling interrupts.

Unthrottling holds the port lock with interrupts saved, restores a mask with timeout and conditional receive as in enabling, writes it to hardware, and when DMA reception is in use reasserts receive enable in DMA control.
Channel shutdown clears break signalling and FIFO enable while preserving other control bits in the supplied line-control register.

UART disabling clears automatic flow status, then under lock preserves modem outputs while keeping the UART and transmit enabled, and finally disables break and FIFOs on receive control and, on split hardware, on transmit control as well.
Interrupt disabling holds the port lock, zeroes the saved software mask, writes the zero mask to hardware, then clears all pending sources with an all-ones value.

Full shutdown disables interrupts, stops DMA, frees the IRQ, cancels both transmit trigger timers after the handler drains, stops RS485 transmission under lock when active, disables the UART, disables the clock, selects pin sleep state, runs optional platform exit, and flushes buffered data when a flush operation exists. The SBSA variant only disables interrupts, frees the IRQ and flushes.

Read and ignore masks derive from termios input and control selections. The read mask always accepts overrun plus low data bits, adding framing and parity when input parity checking is requested and break when any break or mark handling is requested. The ignore mask adds framing and parity for ignore-parity, break for ignore-break with overrun when both ignores combine for raw support, and a dummy receive marker when the receiver is disabled.

Baud selection uses a divisor of eight on oversampling hardware otherwise sixteen, bounding the maximum by the current UART clock or, for reprogrammable clocks, by the rounded maximum rate. The core baud helper picks the rate, an optional clock setter reprograms the clock with error reporting on failure, and DMA poll timing scales inversely with baud when automatic. Some variants skip baud registers entirely, otherwise the divisor is rounded from clock and baud with small decrements for specific high-speed oversampling ranges to avoid start-bit sampling delay.

Frame setup maps size, stop, parity enable with even versus odd, stick parity, and FIFO enable for deep FIFOs into line control. Under lock the driver refreshes the per-port timeout and RS485 drain interval from frame bits and baud, rebuilds status masks, enables modem-status watching per the enable predicate, suppresses hardware flow when RS485 is active, updates CTS and RTS enables with automatic status to match flow selection, adjusts the oversampling factor against baud, programs fractional and integer divisors, then writes line control after the baud registers and re-enables receive.

Modem-status watching is required when the port advertises hard pulse-per-second on carrier, when hardware flow control is selected, or when the local flag is clear. The predicate combines these three conditions disjunctively.

SBSA termios forces the fixed baud in both directions, strips size, stop, parity, stick and flow selections to enforce eight data bits without parity or extra stop or flow, asserts local mode, then under lock refreshes timeout for eight-bit operation at fixed baud and rebuilds status masks.

Type reporting returns the stored driver string for AMBA ports and null otherwise. Port configuration assigns the AMBA type when the type flag is present. Verification rejects mismatched types, out-of-range IRQ numbers, baud bases below 9600, and mapbase mismatches.

RS485 reconfiguration stops an in-progress transmission when the port already runs in RS485 mode, and when the new request enables RS485 it clears automatic RTS enable in hardware and software status.

Two operation tables expose the driver interface. The standard table wires transmit empty, modem set and get, transmit stop and start, receive stop, throttle and unthrottle, modem enable, break control, startup, shutdown, DMA flush, termios, type, config and verify, plus polling init and character access when console polling is configured. The SBSA table reuses transmit and receive controls and type, config, verify and polling hooks, but substitutes no-op modem set and zero-returning modem get, omits throttle and DMA handling, and uses SBSA-specific startup, shutdown and termios.

Observed private state includes a saved interrupt mask, clock handle and sampled UART clock, FIFO depth, modem snapshot, DMA usage and control flags with poll timing, RS485 state and drain timing, trigger timers, console newline tracking, fixed baud for constrained variants, vendor capability flags and inversion masks, plus a global indexed table of port instances sized by the UART count.

Console character output waits for transmit space with CPU relaxation, writes the byte, and records whether the line ended. Option probing returns early when the UART is disabled, otherwise it decodes parity from enable and even-select indications, selects seven versus eight data bits from the length field, derives the divisor from integer and fractional registers or a fixed value when skipped, computes baud from clock and divisor, and doubles it when oversampling hardware reports the factor bit.

Console setup clamps an out-of-range index to zero, looks up the indexed port and fails when absent, selects default pins, enables the clock, marks the line ended, runs optional platform init, samples the clock rate, then either uses fixed options for constrained variants or parses supplied options or probes hardware for baud, parity and bits before applying them. Console exit disables the clock.

Console matching accepts only two names and rejects others, parses early console options into I/O type, address and residual options, requires memory-mapped I/O in either width, then scans the port table for a mapbase match, binds the console to the matching index and runs console setup. Any mismatch returns not-found.

Atomic console emission enters an unsafe non-blocking console region and aborts when entry fails. Unless the variant is always enabled it temporarily enables the UART and transmit while clearing CTS enable, emits a leading newline when the line had not ended and braille mode is off, writes the buffered bytes, spins until the busy indication with vendor inversion clears, restores the prior control when needed, then leaves the unsafe region.

Threaded console emission shares the temporary enable and busy-wait behavior but writes the buffer one byte at a time, cycling unsafe exit and entry around each byte and stopping early when re-entry fails, then re-acquires the unsafe region in a loop before waiting for idle and restoring control.

Two configurations of the braille predicate exist, one reporting true when a console pointer is present and carries the braille flag and the other always reporting false. The unsafe enter and exit helpers in the routed configuration always report failure, so callers treat the region as unavailable.

Port lock discipline uses interrupt-saving acquisition for enabling, unthrottling and both termios paths, and plain interrupt acquisition for startup control programming, UART disabling, interrupt disabling and RS485 stop during shutdown. Quiesce, polling, console probing and console emission do not take the port lock in the shown fragments.

Port identity uses PORT_AMBA. Console matching accepts pl011 and qdf2400_e44 over UPIO_MEM and UPIO_MEM32. Console indexing is bounded by UART_NR with fallback to zero. Default console parameters are 38400 baud, 8 bits, no parity and no flow. Full pending clear uses 0xffff. Port verification requires baud base at least 9600.

Several paths spin with CPU relaxation until hardware clears a flag, including polling and console output waiting for transmit space and console emission waiting for busy to clear. These loops carry no timeout in the shown code and rely on hardware progress.

SBSA operation assumes no modem status lines, fixed eight-bit no-parity single-stop local operation at a fixed baud without flow control, modem set as no-op and modem get returning zero, and no DMA or FIFO trigger programming.
